issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies that Milkable.messageOnMilk() should return a boolean (true if milking was successful, false otherwise). However, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with return type String and implementations (Seal, Goat) return human-readable strings (e.g. "Seal X is milked"). This mismatch will confuse students: following the specification leads to a boolean signature that is incompatible with the provided solution/tests, and following the solution contradicts the written spec.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement to require Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String and adjust the textual description to show returning a descriptive message (e.g. "<Animal> <name> is milked"), or (B) change the solution and template implementations so Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns boolean and adapt tests/output to handle boolean results (and move any human-readable messages to separate methods or printing logic). Ensure template, tests, and documentation all use the same return type.
